clue.text: Ditch exasperated expression Pete's forgotten

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so these words drop from the expression

parts.note: the exclamation 'for Pete's sake!' voices exasperation
taken as written, the possessive name in the exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone is told to drop the weary exclamation they keep making about Pete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgotten' removes the word PETES from FOR PETE'S SAKE, leaving the two outer words joined.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch someone or something is to abandon it, the same as to desert it.

clue.text: Like a summer event: begin with song

parts.note: to open is to begin
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A summer festival starts with a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer concerts and fêtes are often held outdoors.

clue.text: Sauce too reduced in South America

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the shortened word sits inside the abbreviation
reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: A sauce is reduced in a South American kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts the last letter from the synonym for 'too', and 'in' sets what is left within the continent's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy Latin American tomato relish served with tortilla chips.

clue.text: Dresses sank unevenly, stuffed with a newspaper

indicators.note: stuffed with means filled, so the rearranged word holds the other letters
unevenly means irregularly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: Clothes stuffed with a newspaper sank lopsidedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unevenly' turns SANK into KANS, and AFT goes inside after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Long loose tunics of Middle Eastern origin are robes or gowns.

clue.text: For one, golf trophies make breakfast containers

parts.note: 'for one' means for example, abbreviated e.g.
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
trophies are often cups

explanation.surface: A golfer's trophy cabinet is repurposed to hold the breakfast things.
explanation.definitionFit: Small holders for boiled eggs sit on the breakfast table.

clue.text: Sanction a run in souped-up car, a small one for racing

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the car's letters enclose the others

parts.note: GT, Gran Turismo, denotes a high-performance car
to sanction is to approve, OK
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Permission to drive a tuned car on a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands for car: a little racing vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny low motorised vehicle raced around karting tracks.

clue.text: Halfwit hires crooked bolt cutters?

parts.note: a clot is a fool

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool hires dodgy tools for cutting through locks.
explanation.walkthrough: A bolt is a roll of cloth, so makers of clothes cut into bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes makers and sellers cut lengths from rolls of fabric.

clue.text: Salesman delivers this new model

parts.note: a salesman's smooth spiel is his patter

explanation.surface: A salesman presents the latest version.
explanation.definitionFit: A template or design to copy is an example.

clue.text: Lift bottom line up for an LBD, perhaps

parts.note: to cock is to raise, as a dog cocks a leg
the tail is the bottom end
to dress ranks is to line soldiers up

explanation.surface: An instruction to lift something up and line its bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: LBD is short for little black dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A little black frock is the classic example of party evening wear.

clue.text: Very inaccurate story about religious coverage

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the story's word runs backwards

parts.note: an untrue story is a lie

explanation.surface: A newspaper is accused of badly misreporting religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the untrue story backwards; the coverage is a head covering, not press reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuns and many religious women wear a cloth covering over the head.

clue.text: Fellow staggers round firm engaged in making formal wear

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the staggering word encloses the other letters

parts.note: to stagger someone is to rock them
CO is short for company, a firm
to be at something is to be engaged in it, as in 'at work'

explanation.surface: A man reels as he walks around the office of a firm that makes evening dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the firm and 'engaged in' together inside the word for staggers; 'making' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-skirted men's jackets once worn as formal daytime dress for gentlemen.

clue.text: View missing yellow hat

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so these letters drop out of the view

parts.note: a panorama is a wide view
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A view lacks any yellow, or a yellow hat is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes OR, heraldic yellow, from PANORAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A light straw brimmed headwear style traditionally woven in Ecuador.

clue.text: Royal couple precede cook carrying one cover for crown

indicators.note: precede means come in front, so the royals go first in the string

parts.note: K for king and ER for Elizabeth Regina, the queen: two royals

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the cook's word holds the numeral

parts.note: a cook is a chef
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A king and queen walk ahead of a royal chef who is carrying something for the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The crown here is the top of the head, not the regalia.
explanation.definitionFit: A square of cloth tied over the head covers the top of the skull, the crown.

clue.text: Tense French artist shows what's in bottom drawer

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
Henri Rousseau was a French painter

explanation.surface: A nervous French painter is showing his work.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is the British name for a bride's collection of linen and clothes kept for marriage, also called a hope chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's gathered clothes and linen are what she stores up before her wedding.

clue.text: Articles from abroad flank bottom

parts.note: UN is French for a and DER German for the: foreign articles
a flank is a side

explanation.surface: Imported goods are stacked against someone's backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower surface of anything is its base.

clue.text: Nice bloke's casual wear

definitions.meaning: belonging to Jean, a common man's name in France, where the city of Nice is

explanation.surface: A pleasant chap's everyday clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like 'pleasant' but is the French city, so the bloke is a Frenchman called Jean; the possessive reads the same as the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim trousers are the classic informal clothing, and Jean is a typical French forename.

clue.text: Inspect stallion approaching filly's rear

parts.note: a stallion kept for breeding is a stud

indicators.note: rear means the back end, so the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A breeder checks a stallion as it comes up behind a filly.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something closely is to scrutinise it.

clue.text: Hardy girl acquires old place, revealing chest

indicators.note: acquires means takes in, so the girl's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A Hardy heroine buys an old property and finds a treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests a box of treasure but is the torso.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare-breasted, with nothing on above the waist.

clue.text: Perhaps cabaret mystifies housewife

parts.note: to floor someone is to baffle them
HO is short for house and W for wife

explanation.surface: A cabaret act leaves a housewife baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is one example of entertainment staged on a nightclub's dance area.

clue.text: Enjoy longer life not working on river

parts.note: out means not at work, as of strikers
the Wear is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Retirement by a river helps a person live longer.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast something is to survive it, lasting beyond it.

clue.text: Protective wear, more than a couple of lines

parts.note: over means more than
L is short for line, so two make LL

explanation.surface: Work clothes need a little more than two lines of description.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose coat or boiler suit worn to keep clothes clean.

clue.text: Top British runner keeps left

indicators.note: keeps here means stays beside, so the side letter is kept next to the river

parts.note: a river runs, and the Ouse is a British river

explanation.surface: A leading British athlete stays on the left of the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river, a crossword stock trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's shirt is a garment for the upper body.

clue.text: Second pen containing large stone

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the pen holds the size letter

parts.note: Parker is a brand of pen
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A second enclosure holds a big rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like an enclosure for animals; it is the Parker brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a diamond or other glittering gem.

clue.text: Stole hospital garb idiot sent round

indicators.note: sent round means put around, so the idiot's word goes about the garb

parts.note: a twit or tit is a fool in British slang
PPE, personal protective equipment, is what hospital staff wear

explanation.surface: A fool sent around a hospital nicked some protective clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a past tense verb but is the noun, a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape or long scarf worn around the shoulders, as clergy or judges wear.

clue.text: Standard car coat

parts.note: par is the standard level
the Ka is a small Ford car

explanation.surface: An ordinary car coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded windproof jacket of Inuit origin.

clue.text: After start of dissent, see clique split and melt away

indicators.note: after means following, so the anagram comes behind the single letter
the start of a word is its first letter
split means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political clique breaks up and fades once dissent begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' rearranges the letters of 'see clique', and 'After' places them behind the first letter of 'dissent'.
explanation.definitionFit: To become liquid by absorbing moisture, so to dissolve or fade.

clue.text: Bring up sappers and gunners facing backwards

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the army's sappers

indicators.note: facing backwards means turned round, so the gunners' letters run in reverse

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are the gunners

explanation.surface: Army engineers and artillery bring up the back of the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise children is to nurture them to adulthood.

clue.text: Like well-balanced school qualification

parts.note: as means like
level means even or balanced

explanation.surface: A sensible exam result.
explanation.walkthrough: The AS-level is a British exam taken at about seventeen, half an A-level.
explanation.definitionFit: A British pre-university examination taken by sixth-formers.

clue.text: Part of old sewer's altered after collapsing

definitions.note: a part of an old sewing machine, with 's standing for is

indicators.note: collapsing means falling apart, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old drain has been changed since it caved in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain but is one who sews, and the old machines had a foot pedal.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot pedal drove early sewing machines.
